ui.replay.title: Replay theatre
ui.replay.intro: A replay is a saved game that begins at its first tick with its command log still ahead of it. Playback re-simulates the game — which is why it is provably identical, and why any yearly checkpoint can be jumped to directly.
ui.replay.empty: No recordings yet. Any saved game can be turned into one from the save screen.
ui.replay.notVerifiableHint: This build must not judge that recording — verification is version-pinned (format {format}). Watching it is fine.
ui.replay.jumpHint: Yearly checkpoints — these jumps are a plain decode. The bar above reaches every tick in between.
ui.replay.seekExact: This position is checkpoint {year} — the jump only decodes it.
ui.replay.seekResim: {days} game days are re-simulated from checkpoint {year}.
ui.replay.seekLong: {days} game days are re-simulated from checkpoint {year} — this takes a moment.
ui.replay.readOnly: The simulation takes no commands while a recording is playing.
ui.replay.notARecording: That file cannot be opened as a recording:
ui.replay.versionRefused: Verification refused — the recording comes from another version:
ui.replay.notVerifiable: That recording does not say where it ends, so there is nothing to verify:
ui.replay.verify.ok: Verified: the re-simulation reaches the same hash at all {ticks} committed ticks.
ui.replay.verify.divergedAt: Diverges at tick {tick} ({year}) — proven rather than estimated: the re-simulation from tick {from} reaches the recorded state all the way to there, and only this tick leads away from it.
ui.replay.verify.proof: Proof: identical up to tick {tick} ({matched}), and {after} afterwards.
ui.replay.verify.bracket: Diverges somewhere between tick {from} ({fromYear}) and tick {to} ({toYear}). This check does not name an exact tick.
ui.replay.verify.corrupt: Broken recording: the file contradicts itself at {where} (tick {tick}, {year}). That is a damaged FILE rather than a divergent tick, so the simulation is not judged on it.
ui.replay.bracket.multipleCommands: Several command ticks lie in this stretch, and a recording commits to nothing between two checkpoints. Naming one of them would be a guess.
ui.replay.bracket.noCommands: No command lies in this stretch at all, so the divergence cannot be explained by an input — it may have begun at any tick.
ui.replay.bracket.schedule: The command times of this stretch are not the ones the recording committed to — a command was moved, inserted or removed. The file's own tick numbers are therefore no longer evidence.
ui.replay.bracket.logBreak: The command log contradicts its own numbering, so the sequence that ran is not the recorded one.
ui.replay.bracket.uncommitted: The recording committed to no command times for this stretch (an older recording, or a trimmed log). Without that commitment an exact tick cannot be proven.
ui.replay.bracket.unproven: The exact tick could not be proven: re-simulating the stretch did not reproduce the committed state.
ui.replay.corrupt.checkpointDigest: The checkpoint does not match its own hash — payload and commitment are not from the same world.
ui.replay.corrupt.checkpointPayload: The checkpoint's payload is not a readable world standing at that tick.
ui.replay.corrupt.checkpointUnreachable: No re-simulation reaches this committed state, although the same re-simulation hits a later committed state exactly.
ui.replay.break.tickOrder: Log entry {index} (tick {tick}, no. {seq}) sits before its predecessor — the order was changed.
ui.replay.break.sequence: Log entry {index} (tick {tick}) carries no. {seq} and does not follow its predecessor — a command was inserted or removed.
ui.replay.break.schedule: Between tick {from} and tick {to} the command schedule differs from what the recording committed to.

ui.handbook.title: Handbook
ui.handbook.time.title: Two clocks
ui.handbook.time.body: Vehicles move in real time: twenty simulation steps a second. The calendar runs separately - a game day is ten seconds, a game year an hour. Production, growth, ageing and the books all hang off the calendar, not off driving time.
ui.handbook.camera.title: Camera
ui.handbook.camera.body: Drag with the right mouse button to move the map, scroll to zoom. A click on the overview map jumps straight there, and so does a row in any list.
ui.handbook.firstLine.title: The first line
ui.handbook.firstLine.body: Two towns, a road between them, a stop at each end, a depot and two buses. It is the cheapest line in the game and it pays for itself in two to four game years.
ui.handbook.assistant.title: The route assistant
ui.handbook.assistant.body: The assistant finds the route itself, goes around obstacles and builds bridges and tunnels only where nothing else will do. Press M to turn it off and lay exactly the line you drag. The preview shows the cost, the length, the gradient, the tightest curve and the speed that follows from it before you commit.
ui.handbook.gradients.title: Gradients
ui.handbook.gradients.body: One height level is eight metres. Over a fifty metre tile that would be 160 per mille, which no rail type will climb. Gradients are therefore measured over a window: spread the climb across several tiles and the train goes up it.
ui.handbook.stations.title: Stations are modular
ui.handbook.stations.body: Platforms, stops, quays and runways within four tiles of each other are ONE station with one shared cargo pool. That is exactly how a transfer point is made: the lorry sets down, the train picks up.
ui.handbook.blockSignal.title: Block signal
ui.handbook.blockSignal.body: A signal divides the line into sections. A train claims the section ahead of it whole or waits. With no signals the whole line is one section and only one train runs.
ui.handbook.passingLoop.title: Passing loop
ui.handbook.passingLoop.body: Two tracks side by side, joined at both ends - and a signal immediately past each merge. Without those signals the loop is a single section and buys nothing.
ui.handbook.pathSignal.title: Path signal
ui.handbook.pathSignal.body: A station throat with several platforms wants a path signal. It lets a train in as soon as ITS route through the points is clear, instead of locking the whole throat.
ui.handbook.deadlock.title: When nothing moves
ui.handbook.deadlock.body: Two trains meeting nose to nose on single track block each other for ever. The game warns after a minute of standing still and marks them in the F3 overlay. The answer is a passing loop, or making the line one way.
ui.handbook.chains.title: Production chains
ui.handbook.chains.body: Primary industries produce out of nothing; factories need supplying. A factory that is supplied but whose output nobody collects shuts down after 24 months - and takes the line feeding it with it. Finish your chains.
ui.handbook.collection.title: Rating and collection
ui.handbook.collection.body: How much an industry hands over depends on the rating of the stations serving it. A badly rated station gets less cargo - and that is the death spiral: less cargo, fewer visits, a worse rating.
ui.handbook.decay.title: Cargo spoils
ui.handbook.decay.body: Every parcel loses value with time, down to a tenth of its worth. Perishable cargo loses it faster; a cold store at the station stops it entirely. A pile of waiting cargo is therefore not a balance, it is a loss.
ui.handbook.transfer.title: Transfers
ui.handbook.transfer.body: A vehicle loads a parcel only when its next stop is on a shortest route to that parcel’s destination, and sets it down the moment that stops being true. Feeder lines are what those two rules produce. Every leg is paid for exactly the distance it covered.
ui.handbook.revenue.title: What a trip earns
ui.handbook.revenue.body: Revenue rises with distance but less than proportionally - twice the distance does not pay twice. Fast delivery pays; slow delivery falls back towards the floor.
ui.handbook.upkeep.title: Upkeep eats capital
ui.handbook.upkeep.body: Every vehicle and every tile of infrastructure costs money each month whether or not anything runs. A company that only builds is bankrupt in six to nine years. Three months in the red is a warning; twelve is the end of the game.
ui.handbook.council.title: The town council
ui.handbook.council.body: Every town rates every company from 0 to 100: stations and passengers carried lift the rating, track through the streets and demolished houses lower it. At 75 you can buy exclusive building rights; below 25 the town refuses you permits.
ui.handbook.carbon.title: The carbon levy
ui.handbook.carbon.body: From the year 2000 emissions cost money, and more of it every year from 2005. What is measured is the work done, not the distance: a heavy train uphill emits more than the same train on the level. Electrification is subsidised from the same year.
ui.tutorial.title: Tutorial
ui.tutorial.intro: Five lessons. Each one runs in your own game with the ordinary tools - nothing here has to be unlearned later.
ui.tutorial.basics.title: Camera, time, a first bus line
ui.tutorial.basics.intro: Start the clock and connect two towns.
ui.tutorial.basics.step1: Start time with the space bar or the keys 1 to 4.
ui.tutorial.basics.step2: Press S and build a road between two towns.
ui.tutorial.basics.step3: Put a stop at each end.
ui.tutorial.basics.step4: Build a depot and buy a bus.
ui.tutorial.basics.step5: Give the bus both stops as its orders and send it out.
ui.tutorial.rail.title: A first railway
ui.tutorial.rail.intro: Track, platforms, a train and its order list.
ui.tutorial.rail.step1: Press R and drag a line; the assistant finds the route.
ui.tutorial.rail.step2: Build a platform at each end.
ui.tutorial.rail.step3: Put a train together in the engine shed and buy it.
ui.tutorial.rail.step4: Give the train both stations as its orders.
ui.tutorial.signals.title: Signals
ui.tutorial.signals.intro: Why the second train is standing still - and what fixes it.
ui.tutorial.signals.step1: Buy a second train for the same line.
ui.tutorial.signals.step2: Press G and place at least two signals on plain line.
ui.tutorial.signals.step3: Press F3 to see the block overlay and the sections.
ui.tutorial.signals.step4: Get to the point where no train is waiting any more.
ui.tutorial.chain.title: A production chain
ui.tutorial.chain.intro: Forest to sawmill to town, and why cargo must not sit.
ui.tutorial.chain.step1: Serve an industry until cargo is waiting at the station.
ui.tutorial.chain.step2: Carry it away until the industry shows a service figure.
ui.tutorial.chain.step3: Serve it well enough that its production level passes 100 %.
ui.tutorial.chain.step4: Build a station module - a crane, a canopy or a cold store.
ui.tutorial.transfer.title: A transfer point
ui.tutorial.transfer.intro: Lorry feeders onto a freight train at a combined station.
ui.tutorial.transfer.step1: Build a station with at least two modules.
ui.tutorial.transfer.step2: Refit a vehicle to carry something else.
ui.tutorial.transfer.step3: Get at least three vehicles running.
ui.tutorial.transfer.step4: Earn freight revenue in the current financial year.

ui.tooltip.tool.none: Click a tile to inspect it - terrain, town, station, industry. Builds nothing and costs nothing.
ui.tooltip.tool.road: Lays road tile by tile between two clicks, paid per tile. The first road on open land claims the tile for your company; a town's own street stays public.
ui.tooltip.tool.track: Lays rail between two clicks; the assistant finds the smoothest alignment, bridges and tunnels included. Paid per tile, structures extra - and every tight curve limits train speed for good.
ui.tooltip.tool.connect: Picks two stations and plans the complete rail link, the full bill shown before anything is charged - the only build that asks first.
ui.tooltip.tool.stop: Puts a stop on an existing road, or on the free tile beside it - then the driveway to the nearest road is built and paid for with it. It founds a station or joins one close by; the catchment collects passengers and mail, and the rating decides how much of it actually appears.
ui.tooltip.tool.depot: Puts a depot on an existing road, or on the free tile beside it with its driveway built in: road vehicles are bought, serviced and refitted here, and a called vehicle drives back on its own. Costs upkeep every month.
ui.tooltip.tool.platform: Lays a platform on existing track and makes the tile a station where trains load. More platform tiles serve longer trains - a train hanging past the end loads far slower.
ui.tooltip.tool.raildepot: An engine shed on existing track: trains are assembled from traction units and wagons here, serviced and refitted. Costs upkeep every month.
ui.tooltip.tool.quay: A berth on the shoreline for ships. The station centre stays on land, so the catchment keeps the shore it serves - a harbour beside a mine keeps the mine.
ui.tooltip.tool.airstrip: The smallest airfield: one runway, slow turnaround. Aircraft serve any other airfield on the map - no track or road needed in between.
ui.tooltip.tool.airport: A mid-size airfield: two runways and a faster turnaround, so more aircraft per day before the holding stack fills.
ui.tooltip.tool.intlairport: The largest airfield: four runways, the fastest turnaround. Expensive to keep - worth it only where many aircraft meet.
ui.tooltip.tool.shipdepot: A depot on open water: ships are bought, serviced and refitted here. Costs upkeep every month.
ui.tooltip.tool.freightterminal: A goods-yard module beside an existing station: freight loads half again as fast, and one module more lifts the equipment term of the rating.
ui.tooltip.tool.canopy: A roof beside an existing station: +8 rating points on its own, and waiting cargo spoils a third slower under it. Costs upkeep every month.
ui.tooltip.tool.coldstore: A cold hall beside an existing station: perishable cargo stops spoiling here entirely. The steepest upkeep of the three yard modules.
ui.tooltip.tool.signal: Divides plain line into block sections that exactly ONE train may hold. Clicking the same signal again cycles it: both directions, then one way per direction.
ui.tooltip.tool.pathsignal: Reserves only the exact path a train takes through the section instead of all of it - several trains can share a station throat.
ui.tooltip.tool.waypoint: Forces a route through the tile: a marker on track, a buoy on water, a sign on a road. Orders can target it like a station, just without loading.
ui.tooltip.tool.demolish: Removes what stands on the tile and refunds a quarter of the build price. Another company's structures cannot be touched.
ui.tooltip.tool.raise: Lifts a terrain corner one level, paid per moved corner and level - neighbouring corners follow, because no tile may step more than one level. Blocked under track, structures and foreign ground.
ui.tooltip.tool.lower: Digs a corner one level down at the same price per moved corner. Land dug down to sea level floods and becomes navigable water.
ui.tooltip.tool.level: Drags a whole area to one height and charges every corner that has to move. The cheap way to prepare ground for stations - and the expensive way to cross a mountain.
ui.tooltip.status.cash: Liquid money; every build and every month's upkeep comes out of here. {warn} months in the red draw the warning, after {end} months the company is wound up.
ui.tooltip.status.loan: Interest is booked monthly. The limit grows with yearly profit and fixed assets - a company that earns may also borrow more.
ui.tooltip.station.rating: The rating out of 100 IS the share of generated cargo that appears here at all: at 60, forty percent never shows up. The x-ray below prices every term.
ui.tooltip.industry.level: Production level. Twelve well-collected months raise it ten points, up to 200 - and nothing ever lowers it; neglect runs the closure clock instead.
ui.tooltip.industry.stock: Output waiting in the yard, capped at {months} months of the industry's own production - at the cap the works throttles to a standstill until somebody collects.
ui.tooltip.industry.service: Twelve-month mean of what left ON A VEHICLE against production. Eighty percent sustained expands the works; what a station merely piled up counts for nothing.
ui.tooltip.term.wait: Full while the oldest waiting cargo is younger than {good} days, zero from {bad} days. Collect the oldest cargo, not the newest, to recover it.
ui.tooltip.term.frequency: Counts vehicle calls of the last {window} days; {visits} calls reach the full score. More departures help even when each one carries less.
ui.tooltip.term.equipment: Grows with every module beyond the first; a canopy is worth {canopy} points on its own. Building the yard out lifts it.
ui.tooltip.term.reliability: The mean reliability of the vehicles that call here. Ageing, unserviced vehicles drag the station down with them.
ui.tooltip.term.overflow: The malus for cargo turned away at a full station. It fades once the backlog is being collected again.
ui.tooltip.vehicle.age: Age against design life. Past its design life a vehicle pays {factor}x upkeep and loses reliability twice as fast - replace or renew it.
ui.tooltip.vehicle.reliability: Falls with every year in service and recovers in a depot. Low reliability means more breakdowns and a worse rating at every station it serves.
ui.tooltip.vehicle.earned: Lifetime revenue, the yearly rate beside it - hold it against the yearly upkeep above: a line that cannot out-earn its upkeep is a hobby.
ui.tooltip.finance.valueGraph: Company value = cash plus the fleet's book value minus the loan - one point per closed year, the last one is today. Buying a vehicle alone does not move it (money becomes book value); depreciation and profit do.
ui.tooltip.line.networkValue: This line's earned revenue divided by its vehicles' ceiling: capacity x tariff x top speed - what they would take with no loading time and a full load in both directions. Because the ceiling does not depend on the alignment, the percentage measures the network design rather than the size of the fleet. So far {earned} of {ceiling}.
ui.tooltip.finance.networkValue: The whole fleet's earned revenue divided by its ceiling: capacity x tariff x top speed - what the vehicles would take with no loading time and a full load in both directions. The ceiling depends on the vehicles alone and never on the alignment: the whole difference between a smooth, signalled line and a slapdash one lands in the numerator. Parked vehicles count. So far {earned} of {ceiling}.
